newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra to crack down on parliament benefits.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra to crack down on parliament benefits.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Monday his government could crack down on parliamentary benefits after widespread allegations of abuse.
But he stressed most parliamentarians did not abuse their benefits.
"I won't resist if there are proposals to tighten the system," Howard told Sydney radio 2UE.
"I'm prepared to look at changes that improve accountability, but don't impose unreasonable burdens on honest people."
Administrative Affairs Minister David Jull was considering ways of tightening up the system, Howard said.

The possible revamp was sparked by allegations two weeks ago that independent senator Mal Colston had misused his government car and expense entitlements and had given office jobs to relatives who did not actually work.
Colston, on whom the government often relies to get contentious legislation through the non-government dominated upper house Senate, has denied all charges.
But the Australian Federal Police are studying some of the allegations to determine if an investigation is warranted, and Jull's department is also looking at the allegations.

"There may be irregularities in the use of Com (Commonwealth) car in Canberra and his use of hire cars under his charter entitlement, but a more detailed examination is needed," Jull told parliament on February 27.

But Colston has turned on his former Labor Party colleagues -- who have admitted seeking revenge for his defection from the party last August -- hitting them with a "dirt file" of parliamentary privilege abuse cases.
"It's messy because anything that involves allegations of abuse of parliamentary entitlements tends to reflect poorly on all of us," Howard said of the situation on Monday.
"... but my colleagues and I have nothing to hide and can I say, I believe that the great majority of people on the Labor Party side have nothing to hide either."
